font.b: What was the historical context throughout the chain of custodianship?

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe center; width: 311px; height: 1px; padding-top: 450px; margin-left: 202px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: center; max-height: 168px; overflow: hidden; color: #000000;
display: inline-block; font-size: 1px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #000000; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

font.b: Three significant time periods: the crucifixion of Jesus, the destruction of the Jerusalem Temple, and the Bar Kokhba revolt

div.span: From Jesus' ministry (30–33 AD) until the destruction of the Temple in 70 AD, the earliest Christian community existed as a small, multilingual Jewish sect within the Roman Empire. Oral reports about Jesus circulated both publicly and privately and were centered around the Church of Jerusalem.

div.font: After 70 AD, Christianity spread more rapidly across the Roman Empire, shifting from a primarily Jewish and Aramaic context to a predominantly Gentile and Greek-speaking one - even while facing persecution. Written accounts multiplied and circulated during this phase, including traditions that were later deemed heretical.

After the failed Bar Kokhba revolt (132–136 AD), the split between Christianity and Rabbinic Judaism became permanent. Christianity developed a more formal institutional structure, and Church Fathers began defending and consolidating apostolic tradition against rival claims. After Constantine's conversion in 312 AD, Rome emerged as the new capital of Christianity.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe center; width: 311px; height: 1px; padding-top: 450px; margin-left: 517px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: center; max-height: 168px; overflow: hidden; color: #000000;
display: inline-block; font-size: 1px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #000000; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

font.b: Three significant time periods: the time of Quranic revelation, the time of Quranic textual standardization, and the time of Hadith compilation

div.font: The Quran was revealed to Prophet Muhammad over 23 years (610-632 AD, 13 in Makkah and 10 in Madinah) uniting warring, independent tribes into a single nation and extending its message into northern Africa and southern Europe.

div.span: After the Prophet's death in 632 AD, the next 4 caliphs standardized the Quranic text to combat the threat of memorizers falling in battle, as well to ensure its meaning would be consistent among the Arab tribes with different dialects.
After Uthman standardized the Quranic dialect (between 560-656 AD), Islam expanded beyond Arabia, making it harder to verify which reports about the Prophet were authentic.

From 684-915 AD, hadith compilations were written and a formal science of authentication emerged. This period also marked the beginning of the Islamic Golden Age, during which many branches of knowledge - including, but not limited to, Hadith - were developed and systematized.

font.b: What were the standards of testimony and custodianship in this time?

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe center; width: 311px; height: 1px; padding-top: 620px; margin-left: 202px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: center; max-height: 183px; overflow: hidden; color: #000000;
display: inline-block; font-size: 1px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #000000; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

font.b: Eyewitness testimony, gradually shifting towards scholarly textual standardization

div.span: In the 1st-century Jewish context, valid testimony required at least two credible witnesses (free, adult males without conflict of interest), based on Deuteronomy 19:15 and Mishnaic traditions. Roman standards similarly valued reputable eyewitnesses (non-criminals) and oral testimony in court, with writing reserved for limited formal records.

After 70 AD, as Christianity spread under Roman persecution, standards shifted toward Greco-Roman historiography and Jewish diaspora oral practices, resulting in semi-verbatim preservation and the growth of written accounts that defended core narratives against competing versions. From the 2nd-4th centuries, Roman legal writing expanded, while Christian custodianship formalized around three criteria: apostolic origin, catholicity (universal acceptance), and non-contradiction with established faith.

Thus, the Bible's guiding standard was credible eyewitness testimony with faithful transmission of meaning and message, not verbatim memorization. This is reflected in the numerous early textual variants, which arose from scribes attempting to better preserve and transmit the intended truth than the original.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe center; width: 311px; height: 1px; padding-top: 620px; margin-left: 517px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: center; max-height: 183px; overflow: hidden; color: #000000;
display: inline-block; font-size: 1px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #000000; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

span.style: background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(237, 237, 237)); font-size: 8px;

div.span: Pre-Islamic Arabia was a predominantly oral culture that lacked literary and textual presence. As a result, they preserved history through memory, oral performance, and poetic competition rather than writing - which was a skill that was seen as

span.style: background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(237, 237, 237)); font-size: 8px;

div.span: a source of immense cultural pride and honor.

span.style: background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(237, 237, 237)); font-size: 8px;

div.span: Eloquence, genealogy, and precise memorization were central to cultural identity, and written materials - though scarce - were secondary aids to the superior discipline of trained memory.

This same system continued during the Quran's revelation and after, producing mass, communal, verbatim memorization, later mirrored in Hadith sciences as well. Daily prayers, being communal and audible, required Quranic recitation - meaning any mistake could be corrected publicly, reinforcing collective preservation. As a result, the oral Quran functioned as a primary, living authority, while also anchoring its textual standardization and safeguarding its exact wording.

font.b: Is there anything anachronistic (historically or logically out of place) about the claim or its custodianship?

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe center; width: 311px; height: 1px; padding-top: 805px; margin-left: 202px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: center; max-height: 293px; overflow: hidden; color: #000000;
display: inline-block; font-size: 1px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #000000; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.span: Female testimony was not considered credible, yet all 4 Gospels report that the first witnesses of Jesus' resurrection were women.

span.style: font-size: 8px; background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(237, 237, 237));

div.span: Jews and Samaritans were hostile toward one another, yet Jesus is depicted engaging a Samaritan positively.

span.style: font-size: 8px; background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(237, 237, 237));

div.span: Despite purity laws and social boundaries, Jesus is shown dining with, healing, and ministering to those considered "unclean", including tax collectors, lepers, prostitutes, and other outcasts.

span.style: font-size: 8px; background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(237, 237, 237));

div.span: In a culture where superiors would not submit to inferiors, Jesus is baptized by John in an act of symbolic cleansing - despite John being lower in status.

span.style: background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(237, 237, 237)); font-size: 8px;
font-size: 8px; background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(237, 237, 237));

div.span: Although Jewish monotheism rejected the idea that God could be a man, Jesus is depicted as divine - God Himself. However, relative to Greco-Roman beliefs, this claim would not have seemed anachronistic.

span.style: font-size: 8px; background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(237, 237, 237));

div.span: Although Jewish tradition emphasized God's open and jealous self-disclosure, Jesus' divine identity is portrayed as implied or veiled rather than explicit.

div.font: - Although the expected Messiah would triumph, Jesus is portrayed as crucified by Rome - a shameful death reserved for criminals. The resurrection resolves this issue, but the very concept of a dying-rising figure was not unusual in Greco-Roman contexts.

- Despite the expectation that authentic messages would be clear and consistent from the start (and orally transmitted as such), the Gospels appear to reflect a rising Christology, with Jesus's divinity becoming more easily identifiable in later-written texts.

div.span: Notes: Jesus also reinterpreted Jewish understanding of the law (such as being more lenient with stoning, yet more strict with divorce), but these are non-fundamental. Also, regarding the rising Christology: some argue that this sign of changing what Jesus himself claimed, while others defend by defining it as progressive revelation, where different authors highlight different aspects of the complete, unified truth.

font.b: Many examples against the 7th century Arabian context

font.font: - Females were seen as inferior to males, yet the Quran states that men and women are equal under the sight of God
font.span: . When women weren't able to own property, inherit wealth, and consent to marriage, now they can. Where daughters could be buried alive due to her birth dishonoring her family, now that was considered a crime.
an individual's identity, protection, nobility, and honor were entirely dependent on their tribe)
, the Quran states that the most noble in the sight of God are those who are most righteous.

span.font: - Despite Arabian expertise and history of established poetry and eloquence, the Quran's structure does not fall in any prior literary or oral genres.

div.span: Despite the Quran being considered the height of eloquence (even by its opponents), it is attributed to Muhammad - a man known to be illiterate. Yet there are many instances where the verses are immediately revealed in response to live, unpredictable situations - without later revision, proofreading, correction, or alteration to the original words.

font.span: - In a context in which religious scriptures are written by men (and are defended as divinely guided), the Quran claims to be authored by God Himself and
He will be the one to preserve it.

div.font: - Despite being geographically surrounded by polytheists (denying the hereafter), Jews (rejecting an Arab prophet), and Christians (upholding Trinitarian or heterodox views), the Quran proclaims a pure monotheism distinct from all three - though closest in form to Jewish belief.

font.span: Notes: the Quran also reinterpreted Jewish understanding of the law (such as explaining why the laws were so strict) and Jesus' identity as pure human being, but these are non-fundamental. Also, s
ome argue that the Quran's historical and natural claims are uniquely and strikingly consistent with established history and science, but

div.b: What are the weakest links in the strongest chains of custodianship?

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe center; width: 311px; height: 1px; padding-top: 135px; margin-left: 202px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: center; max-height: 253px; overflow: hidden; color: #000000;
display: inline-block; font-size: 1px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #000000; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

font.b: All chains have gaps (either relying on unknown transmission or lost works) except for the Pauline chain

div.font: - Both chains for Mark support the claim that he learned from Peter, but rely on lost work (Papias), an unnamed transmitter, and an unspecified oral tradition.
- The chains for Matthew and Luke both depend on unknown transmitters, and Luke additionally relies on unknown source material.

span.style: background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(237, 237, 237)); font-size: 8px;

div.span: - Note that Matthew, Mark, and Luke state that only the female disciples witnessed the crucifixion (the most important theological event) - meaning that neither Peter (Mark's source) nor Matthew (another disciple of Jesus) witnessed it either.

span.style: background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(237, 237, 237)); font-size: 2px;

div.font: - The chain for John depends on Irenaeus, whose claim for John's authorship relies on Polycarp, who only orally testified this to Irenaeus without writing it in his work.
- John is the only Gospel author who states that he witnessed the crucifixion.

span.style: background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(237, 237, 237)); font-size: 8px;

div.font: - Paul's letters are self-attesting and corroborated by Clement of Rome.
- Ignatius of Antioch also corroborates Paul, but his chain relies on unknown oral transmission.

b.style: background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(237, 237, 237)); font-size: 8px;
font-size: 8px; background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(237, 237, 237));

div.font: - All orthodox-competing chains rely on lost work and unknown oral traditions.
- The Gnostic chain is the exception in that their gospels are preserved, but their chain appears intentionally hidden (according to Irenaeus).
Notes: all chains about the earthly Jesus contain varying degrees of historical uncertainty, with each relying on some unknown or uncorroborated transmission.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe center; width: 311px; height: 1px; padding-top: 135px; margin-left: 517px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: center; max-height: 253px; overflow: hidden; color: #000000;
display: inline-block; font-size: 1px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #000000; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

font.b: The potential weaknesses of the oral and textual chains are mitigated by the other

div.font: - The standardized written text safeguarded by Hafsah is corroborated by mass memorization, while mass memorization is protected from alteration by the standardized text.

span.style: background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(237, 237, 237)); font-size: 8px;

font.span: The more narrators in a chain, the greater the risk of weakness - especially with single-narrator reports (known as ahad hadith).

div.font: - The science of authenticating hadith and examining narrators was established alongside the compilers, allowing hadith narrations to be classified based on their authenticity - and putting more pressure on the compilers for being reliable.

span.style: background-color: transparent; color: light-dark(rgb(0, 0, 0), rgb(237, 237, 237)); font-size: 8px;

div.span: Reliability is tied to the infallibility of the narrators, which is unfalsifiable and supported by fewer corroborating chains than in Sunni transmission - leaving greater room for weakness.

div.font: Notes: the Quran appears to be reliably preserved in history (verified at a later step), while Hadith reliability is dependent on the strength of its compilers and methods.
